801.t: Father's bands: Sam Morgan, Wooden Joe, Superior, Olympia

801.q: Yeah. Yeah. Well, you see, Simon was being the oldest boy. Oldest boy, yeah. Papa used to take him on the job. Right. He used to tell Papa was the baby.

801.s: Eddie says he last played with the Young Tuxedo band. He lists the Black Diamond Band's members, how the Island Queen job broke it up, and a cousin's reuse of the Golden Rule name. Jack Carey then took him to Montgomery.
801.q: Who was I playing with? Yeah. When I quit? Uh-huh. I was playing with, no, it wasn't Chris Kelly. Did you tell you about this? No. I was playing with a young tuxedo band.

801.s: Eddie says he drifted from band to band with no regular one, his last being the Golden Rule around 1921-22 with the same group. He criticizes a book's claims about a manager.
801.q: 20. 21. Nearly 22. Man. So. The same bunch. Trahi. Loicontra. Paul. Born. Old Forsy. Now he told a. Big lie too. I read a piece in that book. About Old Forsy. Say he was the manager. He had to go on the move man. We pick up oil.

476.t: Joining August Sosia's band and its personnel
476.s: After Maurice, Harry played in August Sosia's band; he lists its sax, trombone, trumpet, clarinet, drums, piano and bass players, and Chick (Eddie Palud).
476.ch: Early bands around Bay St. Louis
476.q: I think the four hours, that was in 20... 26, 25. Must have been earlier. About 25. And you were quite a youngster then. Oh yeah. I was a youngster because I wasn't married then.

245.s: Durand led a band with Willie Humphrey, whose grandfather Jim taught Durand. He names the members.
245.q: Well, in Durant and Humphrey band? Mm-hmm. We had, uh, Bebe Mathis on drum. Willie, uh, Buddy Johnson, trombone, I'm playing trumpet. Willie Humphrey, clarinet. And a fellow by the name of Green playing banjo. And, uh, Jimmy Johnson was playing bass. Mm-hmm. Oh, we had a wonderful band. Pretty good…

245.t: Imperial and Onward Brass Band personnel lists
245.s: The second interviewer reads the Imperial and Onward lineups while Durand corrects.
245.q: No, no, that's come to me now. Imperial bass drum. Imperial bass drum.

880.t: Identifying the Professor Holmes band photo from Lutcher
880.s: Looking at a photo of the Holmes brass band of Lutcher, Joseph names the members and instruments.
880.q: Now this guy here, we used to call him Nug. He's got one hand, that's all I've been known. That's the only name. And he was a bass drum player. Bass drum player. John Porter's brother, he's Joe Porter. Cornet. Second, second cornet. Floyd Jackson, bass player. David Jones, I know you heard of him.

880.t: Members of the Holmes Band of Lutcher photo
880.s: Joseph and the interviewers identify players in a photo of the Holmes Band: the one-handed bass drummer John Porter, Floyd Jackson, Davy Jones, Henry Sawyer, Dennis Harris, and cornetists Professor Holmes and Joe Poehler.
880.q: He beat it. He had a hook. The right hand is missing. Yeah that's right. Right hand is missing. All them guys are musicians. John Porter.

178.t: The Moonlight Serenaders and their personnel
178.s: Ferbos and Dejan reconstruct who played in the next band, mostly stock orchestrations.
178.q: Yeah. He kept the Navi Moonlight Center. And then all night they'd been over again. Yeah. And then Tibor Briscoe playing saxophone. Old man Bill, he's working at Crouse playing bass. And Neumon Reese playing drum. He's with Brunus' band now. Oh yeah. And Aston Murray playing piano. No it wasn't…

178.t: Nat Story, the King brothers and Robichaud's band
178.s: They recall Nat Story, trombone-playing brothers, Albert Snyder and Joe Robichaud's band.
178.q: I met his brother and he said, one of them, he was playing trombone with him, playing

118.t: Recording note and Williams's current band at Leroy's
118.s: Russell notes the date, place and tape; Williams names the members of his band at Leroy's.
118.q: Willie Joss, Josh Willis at least. You know Josh Willis the trumpet man? Uh-huh. And Marvin, Tram Martin, Justin Joss on the drum. And then McNeil Groh was on the bass.

118.t: Group at the Caledonia and Decatur Street music
118.s: Williams' group with Kid Howard's, the Jones brothers and Norman Blaze; Decatur and Charter Streets had more music than Bourbon.
118.q: Sure, I had a group there too. Who was in your group at that time? Well I was in my group and Norman Blaze, which some of you jazz people never heard of I don't think, Eulett Jones, Herbert Jones, and Ryber Jones. Those boys there played on Boynton Street in their life.

430.t: Lineups of the Imperial, Superior and Eagle bands
430.s: He recalls the members of the Imperial, Superior and Eagle bands as he first heard them.
430.q: No, I couldn't recall who was in the, Maple Leaf. Only for Supreme Band and Maple Leaf Band, I couldn't recall. But I could give you the lineup of, like, the Eagle Band and the Superior Band, the Olympia Band and Imperial Band, those bands.

430.t: Chip and other local musicians, drummers and trumpeters
430.s: Barbarin names Chip, Mack Murray, Walter Brundy, Tick Chambers and others, often unsure who played with whom.
430.q: Chip, he was a trumpet player, but now he plays, I think he threw around the base now. He racks ball up on Rampart and he ran, I think it is. He ran, yeah. Oh yeah. Yeah. Should have shot by. He was a good man.

250.t: Scrapbook: school band and the Optimist Jazzers lineup
250.s: A school band photo, a Mardi Gras picnic, and his best men Earl Christian and Bill Voorhees.
250.q: That was a school band and we had to use everybody in the school. We couldn't get any ringers. But you had a few good musicians there. This King guy used to arrange for a blue opera, one of them. Dr. Fatter on the tuba. You know Dr. Fatter was in the Clay Shaw case? No, I heard about him.

250.t: Scrapbook: Audubon tea room, first Red Hot groups and jazz club photos
250.s: Photos of his first bands under his own name, recordings, a jazz club broadcast and advertising slogan.
250.q: This was at the Thorngarals. Frank Clark played a pretty good piano. Yeah, and this kid here was AJ Salaci. That was the last time I used him once and I was seeing old Gene and Bazley on the drum.

827.s: Looking at the Peerless band picture, they discuss who led it and identify the Gaspards, Piron, Charlie McCurdy, and Andrew Kimball as trumpeter.
827.q: I don't really remember who was the leader of the band, but most of the time in the days when he was playing the trumpet player always was leading the band.

827.t: Date and setting of the picture at Racket Park
827.s: They date the photo before 1916 and Arthur says it was taken at a picnic at Racket Park, where a lacrosse-like game was played; guitarist unknown.
827.q: He just liked that when he died, yeah, during 1916. But this picture was way a little while before he died. A little while earlier than that you think of? Yeah, yeah, way before he died. This was when they had this, this park was an old park they had back, if I'm not mistaken, around the old Racket…

921.t: Father's height and the Tom Anderson photograph
921.s: Russell checks a photo taken at Tom Anderson's; she confirms it is her father, short like herself, with Louis Russell on piano.
921.ch: Pictures and memories of her father
921.q: That's a perfect picture of him. Yes, it's him. That looks just like him, you say. And that other one is a good picture. It's quite clear.

921.t: More photographs, Ledger Conyers and dating the picture
921.s: They look at other photos, name Ledger Conyers, and date the Tom Anderson picture to the early 1920s.
921.ch: Pictures and memories of her father
921.q: And this is another good picture of him. It's not in uniform there, but that's a good one.

864.t: First bands: Pellis Band and Cornish's band
864.s: The six-piece Pellis Band was his first real band; he then joined Cornish's band on sax and played with Jack Carey.
864.q: Lorenzo, yeah. Well, by that time I had got to playing pretty good. Then I went and played with, we made up another band, Pellis Band. That was the first real band we made up, you know? And we played Rania and made pretty good hits.

864.t: Band with brother-in-law Alan Gaudette after Jack Carey
864.s: After leaving Jack Carey he formed a band with his brother-in-law, trumpeter Alan Gaudette, Joe Avery and others; Gaudette taught many younger players.
864.q: Well after I left Jack, me and my brother in law made up a band called it. We had me on sax and clarinet and my brother in law on trumpet. And we had Joe Avery on trombone. And Sammy Penns on drums. We used my cousin a couple of times on banjo. We had Sammy Penns on banjo. Baptiste? Yeah we used…

268.s: Around the time of his day job he joined Bocage's six-piece band, whose members he lists and who later left or died.
268.ch: Day job, war and Bocage's band
268.q: Outside of Bocci. You started with Bocci then? Yeah, I started with Bocci. At the same time? Well before I was playing with different bands, you know, spot jobs. And then I started, after Newman died, but Pete hired me.

268.t: Regular bands and playing with Louis Dumaine
268.s: He lists his regular bands, mentions Sidney Desvigne, and says he worked with Louis Dumaine before Sonny South.
268.q: That was Sidney, Sidney Desmond. He got a 11 piece band too. Did you play with them too? You know, substitute, because you piano play. I never was a regular man in this band. But my regular band that I really played in was Sonny South Syncopators, and Creole Serenators, Willow County Rippers, and…

775.s: He lists the sidemen in the band including guitar, piano, alto saxophone and drums, with himself on bass.
775.q: Yeah, Earl Barnes was playing, uh, alto. And, uh, we had, uh, Joe Rainey on drums. And, uh, we had, uh, myself on bass. After I got off trumpet. Got on bass. And, uh, let me see who else we had. We had a trauma on clear. Yeah, we had, uh, oh, I'm trying to think now who we had on trauma on, in the…

775.t: Never played with Petit; Sam and Isaiah Morgan bands
775.s: He never played with Petit but did with Rena, Kelly and the Morgans; Isaiah took over after Sam was paralyzed; he had his own band under his name.
775.q: No, Buddy, I never got a chance to play with Buddy in the band. I played with Renny, Chris Kelly, Sam Morgan, Isaiah Morgan, and those fellas.

571.t: Playing in the Eureka Brass Band in the early 1920s
571.s: Willie Parker put George in the Eureka band; he names the older members and the marches they played.
571.ch: George Lewis's first bands and instruments
571.q: Slide. Playing Slide. And a fellow by the name of Smith was playing Tramon. He was the manager of that band. He died too. And an old fellow by the name of Verrett was playing bass. And Alphonse, I can't call his other name, he was playing, he was a dog fellow, he was a pigeon toe playing the…

571.t: The St. Peter's band with Arnold DePass
571.s: The interviewer asks about Arnold DePass's band; Lewis names a few members in garbled text.
571.q: It was his band. It was Elvin Coward. It was Benny Pinnum. It was bamboo I tried more. And, uh, six pieces, seven pieces, whenever they had a piano. Black in San Diego was a piano player. And when that piano was organized, I didn't know who played with it. I know people who played with them for a…

41.t: Photo tour: Paul Mares, Brunies, Rappolo, Sharkey, Monk Hazel, Fazola
41.s: Mares describes the big photos on the wall, led by Paul and the New Orleans Rhythm Kings, with Brunies, Rappolo, Sharkey, Hazel and Fazola.
41.q: Well, of course, facing us here, Bill, is the old New Orleans Rhythm Kings. Brother Paul was the leader of that outfit, which I think was the greatest white band to ever sit on a bandstand. That's not only my opinion. That's the opinion of a lot of the greats if you talk to them. And, of course, up…

41.t: More photos: Girard, Wingy, Barbarin, Oliver, Armstrong, Chink Martin, first Rhythm Kings
41.s: Mares names more pictures, including the first small Rhythm Kings band with Rappolo, Pettis and Schoebel, and Armstrong's Hot Five.
41.q: Because naturally we've got little Georgie Girard here. He's passed on a few years back. I thought Georgie could have been one of the big names in our music if he'd have lived. But just one of the unfortunate things. But those things happen. Now, above Georgia, we've got old Wingy Minhoom.…

970.t: Identifying WPA banjo players, trumpets and other members
970.s: They name Landry, Andrew Morgan, Mike Lane on banjo, Sidney Cates, Leo Sanjay, Glapio, Crawford, Henry Russ, Louis the Man and McCullen, with Paul failing to recall some names.
970.q: Mm-hmm. Suzaphone. You know this fellow here? That's, uh, the old man there. Used to play in the WPA man. He died. And, uh, Suzaphone? Let me... Yeah, I can't think of his name. Um... He died.

970.t: More unrecalled names, Shots and Hoods the banjo player; 111 musicians
970.s: Paul struggles over names, finds Shots and the tall banjoist Hoods, and notes there were about 111 musicians on the project.
970.q: Isn't Fernandez? Isn't Fernandez? No, no, not Fernandez. Uh, him and Padua, they're two good friends. They play jobs together. When he can't make it, Lionel, Lionel something. I can't think of his name, his right name.

839.s: French lists E-Van's sidemen: his brother, Irvin and John Joseph, Walter and Fred Beats, and the interviewer places them today.
839.q: Well, he had his brother on drums, and Irvin Joseph, and John Joseph, a fella by the name of Walter. I forgot the fella named Fred Beats, it's been so long.

839.t: Playing with George Lewis, Sonny Henry and Al Morgan
839.s: French recalls Lewis, Sonny Henry the trombonist and bassist Al Morgan, all linked to Rena's band.
839.q: I played with George Ritz a lot. I played in the band with Sonny Henry and all them different things. We rode it across the river.

734.t: Bands he played with: Lewisty Man, Dusen, Carey, Humphrey
734.s: He considers himself a member only of Lewisty Man's band but played with Dusen, Carey, Percy, and Earl Foster.
734.q: Well, Frankie Dewson, uh, uh, I never did play with his, his band, but I played, he played on, on Lewisty Man's band, see? Well, he was with Lewisty Man. Yeah, he was with Lewisty Man. Me and Lewisty Man and, uh, and Wilkin LaBeth. You remember Wilkin LaBeth? Yes.

734.t: Jack Carey's band members and the Gabriel band
734.s: Zeb on clarinet and Mutt on cornet in Jack Carey's band; Punch known from the country; Gabriel quit.
734.q: Yeah, yeah. Zeb. And I can't think of his... Who was the coronet? What's that fellow's name? Didn't he have a brother? Oh, Mutt.

628.s: They identify the men in a brass band photograph, including Kid Howard, Jim Robinson, Harrison Bradley, Tats Alexander and Noon.
628.q: Uh-huh. Was that a pretty steady standard band or did you use different bands? Wasn't that? Yeah, yeah.

628.t: Photos of his bands and the Lucky Pair
628.s: Looking at photos, Williams identifies his lineup with Eddie Pearson, Jimmy Clayton, Father Al and Andrew Morgan, and a regular uniformed band that started at the Lucky Pair.
628.q: No, a regular lineup, regular bands. See we got uniforms. We started on at the Lucky Pair. Where's that? The Lucky Pair was at Dolphin and Congress. The Lucky Pair. Mm-hmm. The Lucky Pair.

432.t: Ridgley's band, Don Albert and John Porter
432.s: He recalls Ridgley's band lineup, how Don Albert stripped it and John Porter.
432.q: Yeah. And what about Ridley's band? Well Ridley, I played with Ridley, returned to houses, all uptown, and Emma Barrett was playing And Emma Barrett was playing in that band, and Gilbert Young was playing in that band, and Happy was on drums, Happy Goldston was playing drums. And I believe I saw…

432.t: Playing with Papa Celestin and his sidemen
432.s: He recalls working with Celestin, who had Howard Davis, Harrison Brett and Gabriel in his band.
432.q: No, I played with him, you know how Celestan was. He kept a fellow a while, you know when he had jobs, you know what I'm saying? I worked with him a while and then after winding up, he wound up with Albert French.

279.t: Picnic bands and the Owls at the Halfway House
279.s: He recalls pickup bands and joining the Owls Orchestra with Eddie Miller and Bill Padron.
279.q: Um, well, uh, pick up bands, Dick. Nothing in particular. You know in those days, somebody called you up for a job. You never cared. You didn't much care, no matter who it was. It was just the idea that you had a, you were going to play out at a picnic. And you didn't pay much attention to really…

279.t: Johnny Harmon, Horace Diaz and Vic Pellegrini
279.s: More piano players, including Horace Diaz and Vic Pellegrini, and Diaz at the Silver Slipper.
279.q: I can't remember too well if I worked any jobs with Johnny in those days. I knew of Johnny and had met him and certainly talked with him many times. I can't recall playing any early jobs with Johnny until our association in 1946 at WSMB radio station.

800.t: Sidney Desvigne's band size and Poisey Seville
800.s: Desvigne's band had 10 to 12 pieces; Poisey Seville on banjo and Lewis Nelson on trombone are recalled.
800.q: that piece of you know how many pieces that Sidney had the band when I went out in the Navy band yeah you know he's in the Navy band Sidney had about 12 yeah well when he used to play a

800.t: Personnel of Manuel Perez's Roof Garden band
800.s: He lists the band members: Maurice Durand, Eddie Cherie, a banjo player, Oil Humphrey on trombone, and bass player Kimball, struggling to recall others.
800.q: Oh, they had Des Dune, not Des Dune. Maurice Durand. Eddie Cherie. Eddie Cherie was playing tenor. Tenor and Clannet. Yeah, I was playing Alton and Clannet. We had Kaffer who was playing banjo. And Mercy D, we used to play piano, but she quit. And the school professor. I see all the blanchets. I…

570.t: Photo of Kid Thomas's band and Penn's old drums
570.s: Penn identifies the musicians in a postwar photo of Kid Thomas's band at the American Legion Hall and describes his drum set with a cloth on the bass drum.
570.q: Well, that's one of the Vinette brothers. They have a couple of them play music. Well, that's the trumpet player of the Vinette.

570.s: Names members of Jewel Barnes' band: Big Washington, Mutt Carey, Zeb, Tom Harris; he stayed about three years.
570.q: Well, most of them now is dead, but I do remember that Edwin Washington, you know Washington. Oh yeah, he was there. Big Washington. Big Washington. Yeah, Big Washington.

877.s: Handy names Rhapsodians members: Kerry Levine on sax, a trumpeter Johnny, Frog (Waldron Joseph) on trombone, Lucky on trumpet, Earl on piano and Jimmy on steel guitar.
877.q: Many of the members? Uh, Kerry Levine was a saxophone player. He was a sweet saxophone player. Very young. He was about 19 or 20. He was very young. And, uh... We had another one about the name of... I can't recall his name now, but he was a sweet alto also. And... Little Johnny, or Johnny or…

877.t: Other local bands and Sambo Joseph
877.s: Handy played with local bands like The Chic, with Sam (Sambo) Joseph, Sheik and Kildee, but cannot recall all the names.
877.q: Not with me during those times. During those times. And I played with little local bands, such as The Chic and... And this fellow with blue so large, Sam... Sam who? Sam...

778.t: Identifying musicians in a band photograph; sound check
778.s: Sadie and Allen identify men in an old photo (Faso, George Washington, Leon Rene, Chester, Edmond Hall); then they check the recording.
778.q: Okay Sadie, what's today's date? Today is December, it's 11th, 1984. 1984, okay. Let me see now. I had a photograph I wanted to show you. You know any of those guys? I'm pretty. I played with his band. Yeah, do you know the drummer here? That's Chani? No, that's not Chani and him. That's Faso.…

778.t: Arthur Durbin's and other New Orleans bands booked into Pensacola
778.s: The undertaker booked New Orleans bands, with Sadie on piano; she recalls Arthur Durbin's band and Kid Rena.
778.q: Well we had an Undertaker who used to book all the bands out of New Orleans there. And I always was the piano player with them.

284.s: Clarinet, trombone and bass players who passed through Rena's band while he was in it.
284.q: When I first went in the band, the clarinet player was Zeb, you call him, but what does Zeb, do you know his last name? I know his name but I just can't think of him. Most people don't even know, they just say Zeb until they know. I'll tell you who knows his name and remember his name, it's Happy.…

284.t: Arnold DePass's Olympia Band and its players
284.s: Discussion of the Olympia name from Keppard, its musicians Shots and Henry Julian, and the few jobs he played.
284.q: See, but I didn't play with him too long. I couldn't, I think, I don't think I played with him all over four months. And in that four months, the kind of band he had, well, it was, the band wasn't playing as often as bands like Randy's band. No, no. So in that four months time, I played, four…

883.t: Banner Band members and locating Gus Fontenette
883.s: She names Banner Band members including Weegee Payne, William Williams and the Adam brothers, and they discuss where Gus lives for a future interview.
883.q: So I don't know, I don't forgot where he was from. Let's see, all I know was that this was the old Banner Band, I can call some of them. Oh yeah, that's a funny one. Gestalt Fontenet and Gestalt Fontenet and let's see, where else? So.

883.t: Marriage and the Lake Charles band's members
883.s: They married in New Iberia in 1932. She recalls Bunk as second trumpet in Babin's band, with Skinner Lutcher on bass and Nellie Lutcher on piano.
883.q: Yeah, well that's where the band where I met him, where he came to. And he was playing second trumpet then, because this fellow, Harold, I forgot his name, Charlie, Charlie something, I don't know his last name, but he was playing first trumpet.

780.s: He lists the players: Big Boy Myles, Nolan Blackwell, Alfred Bernard, David Lastie, Warren Miles, Alfred Woodard, Bannister, Edgar Miles and drummer Eric Warner.
780.q: Well, we all just played different instruments, fooling around more or less. But I can't remember all the guys that was in the band at the time. See, there was Nolan Blackwell. Nolan Blackwell.

780.t: Who played on the Chess records
780.s: He tries to recall sidemen including Snooks Eaglin, Big Boy Myles, David Lastie and a forgotten saxophonist.
780.q: Eglin, I think. Ferdinand Eglin, I think. Oh, the, oh. The blind guy. The blind guy. Yeah. Oh, yeah. Yeah. Oh, yeah. Oh, yeah. Oh, yeah. Oh, yeah.

798.t: Identifying people in a photograph of the later Tonic Triad
798.s: Looking at a photograph, Clark identifies Pritchett, the Hamiltons, Oscar Henry, Albert Francis, Peter Rayfield and others.
798.q: Charlie. We can move this. Go, go, go there and get that picture hanging up over there. Tony, that's not the old Tony tried. What year? Oh, I don't know, this was a year. The hair that colored there.

798.t: The Tonic Triad band and its members and instruments
798.s: Clark names the Tonic Triad, how the Depression ended it, and lists members and what they played.
798.q: I have the picture of some of it up there. The late Tonic Triad, not the original Tonic Triad. I have a picture of the late Tonic Triad. Well after the Depression, you know, those fellas, they didn't have no money, you know, no job or nothing. The man just lost all interest in music. So I was lucky…

296.s: He names cornetist Oscar Giovanni and recalls six or seven young cornets, few trombones and many drummers, but few other names.
296.q: Oh, some of them all dead. This fella, Giovanni, he went away from you. He must be dead too.

296.t: Onward Band personnel: Perez, Gaspar, Johnson, Alexander, Matthews
296.s: The interviewer reads off a photo's lineup and Barbarin confirms who played, including Vic Gaspar, Buddy Johnson's brother and Adolph Alexander.
296.q: He played, yeah. He played with you lately. Mm-hmm. He died, uh, about a year, two years.

909.s: Recording pauses while a ballpark band photograph is fetched and the group studies instruments and members including Dumaine.
909.ch: Playing with Punch Miller and touring
909.q: Let's see there. Let's see there. Let's see there. Let's see there.

909.t: Photograph: the band, Shatz and Dumaine
909.s: Morris praises the band, identifies Shatz and director Louis Dumaine; the photo is dated January 15, 1935.
909.ch: Playing with Punch Miller and touring
909.q: Oh, we had a wonderful band there. Woo! People used to come from everywhere just to hear that band.

299.t: Richard McLean names the musicians in the WPA band photo
299.s: Richard McLean and Allen identify band members in the large photo, many names garbled, including Louis Dumaine, Willie Humphrey, Joe Howard and the father himself as a boy.
299.q: They did a variety of things. I guess you can call all these names, couldn't you? Yeah, sure you got it here. See this is Turo, Colin Picksback Turo.

299.t: Finishing the WPA photo: trumpets and other names
299.s: They finish naming the trumpets and others in the picture, including George McCollum, Louis Dumaine and Gilbert Young.
299.q: And Henry Russ, that's why I couldn't call his name. Yeah, that was all I know. Henry Russ and Ricard. Yes, yeah. And Ricard, Ricard, Gilbert Young. Ricard was playing trumpet. And Kid Shots.

832.t: Leading bands in 1922 and forming his own band
832.s: He names Celestine, Kid Rena, Sam Morgan and Andrews as the leading bands, then lists the men in his own band, including Andrew Anderson, James Miller, Willie James and Austin Young.
832.q: I had the same couple of players, Andrew Anderson. You understand? Andrew Anderson. James Miller on piano. And Willie James on classical saxophone. And this boy, Austin Youngs, that's the bass player.

832.t: Identifying the drummer in the old photograph
832.s: They try to name the drummer in the photograph with Buddy Petit, a brother of Rickard Alexis from Bay St. Louis, and whether Edmund Hall was a regular member.
832.q: You were singing? I hadn't started playing drums. You hadn't started playing drums. I hadn't started playing drums. Who was playing drums? I wasn't playing drums. I was singing. The boy is gay, boy. Yeah. Well, I don't call him. I don't remember now. I forget. Rick Carl's brother.

198.t: Working with Bunk; the Imperial and Superior bands
198.s: Barnes worked with Bunk after Bunk got him his clarinet, lists men in Bunk's band, and the group sorts out the Imperial and Superior bands and Jimmie Noone.
198.q: Oh yeah. I worked with Bunk after that. He used to talk about us. Tell me all the time. He brought up with me. He used to say, well, you wouldn't have saw that you'd be playing. I bought a clarinet for a year and you'd be playing with me today. That's true. I was playing with Bunk. I was playing…

198.s: Barnes played with Kid Thomas early on; they list clarinetists in Thomas's band, including Paul Barnes.
198.q: Yeah I played pretty good with Thomas in the early days. I played cards with them quite a while. I don't remember Thomas having any other clarinet play. Just late, just a couple of years back, he's been having different one playing.

177.t: The Sam Morgan band and its later roughness
177.s: Sam and Isaiah Morgan's trumpets, the original personnel, and how the band got rougher when Isaiah took over.
177.q: Izel. Oh, Izel took it there. Before Izel took it. Oh, you see Izel was playing second trumpet, what they called second trumpet, but in their band Sam and Izel made the same thing. It was great. Two great men to make the same thing at the same time. I never could understand. It was great. It wasn't…

177.s: Jiles subbed for Kid Rene's drummer; the band's personnel are named and the reel ends.
177.q: kid Rene? Did you ever know him? Oh yeah. I worked often and on when Joe was sick or he had two jobs. I worked with Rene, Kid Rene. They have a pretty good band? Yeah, yeah. Great band. And they had one of the top bands. Who was in it? Well Eddie, trombone player, Peter Pappy, playing clarinet.…

58.t: Sidney Bechet and the 1925 band with Johnny and Baby Dodds
58.s: Miller recalls playing with Bechet and says his 1925 band included Ory, Dodds and Lorenzo Staulz.
58.q: Pils? Well, it wasn't much to Pils. Wasn't much to Pils. Now I'll tell you a fella, I don't know about, I didn't hear him here, but he fun, you have to tell me, but he played a lot of clarinet. That was this B-guard, where he was Duke. Now I'll tell you who I played with here before he left a…

58.t: Personnel of the band that played blues in the street
58.s: Miller and Allen try to name the trombones, baritone, alto, clarinet and trumpet players in that band, including Pills and Eddie Jackson.
58.q: We had, uh, Big Connie on trombone. Gus and Mad Cat on baritone. There's another trombone in there. Connie? I think Frank Adduce.

896.t: Jack Carey's band: personnel and towns played
896.s: Names the six-piece band: Carey and Punch on trumpet, Babe Joseph Phillip on bass, drummer Voynell Joseph at times, and clarinetists Burbank and Georgia Boy.
896.ch: Early music and the Jack Carey band
896.q: How big the band was? No more than six pieces. Six. Six pieces. Well, Jack Carrey and the same fellow that going trumpet now, Punch. Oh, Punch, yeah. He was going trumpet.

896.t: Kid Rene's band and its clarinetists
896.s: He played with Kid Rene, whose bassists included Chester and Simon, whose style was the same Dixieland, and whose regular clarinetist was Zeb Le Norris.
896.q: Different style? No, it was no different style in the playing. It was no different style in the playing at all. It was the same Dixieland jazz. Yeah.

309.t: Musicians in his father's band: Pick, Selby Thomas, Alonso
309.s: He names players in his father's band and describes the young trumpeter Alonso and Tom Albert replacing him.
309.q: Frank Toast, he played with my daddy. And there was a fellow, they called him Pick, he used to play guitar with my daddy. And Selby Thomas, he was a bass player from the day. See, my daddy, my daddy was playing violin and he had this fellow Selby Thomas. And Selby Thomas, he was playing bass. And,…

309.t: Musicians he worked with: Hood, Eddie Johnson and Sidney Cates

238.s: After a tape fault the interview redoes the band personnel: the Williams brothers, Al Wilson, Collins, Eldridge Joe, Snake Griffin and Lawrence Emerson.
238.ch: Imperial Orchestra and Southern Rhythm Boys
238.q: The personnel consisted of a -- let's see, there were brothers, there were two brothers from Texas, Leo Williams and Eddie Williams. Leo played trombone. Eddie Williams played bass violin, and then we had Al Wilson, who was a marvelous saxophonist and arranger. And he taught me, I studied arranging…

86.t: Basie personnel when Edison came to New York
86.s: Edison lists trumpeters Bobby Moore and Taddy Smith, Claude Williams, Eddie Durham and Buster Smith.
86.q: No, no. That was before. I joined the band in New York. Well, Lips and all of them went in the band in the Grand Terrace. But I -- when we went to New York, Lips got -- you know, he got something going of his own so he left the band. And that's when they got Bobby Moore and then they had another…

171.s: Dance shows a photo of a band under Howard Callender; Ramey is unsure whether he was in it and calls them marching-band musicians.
171.ch: New York: 52nd Street and Lester Young
171.q: The guy that took my place was -- well, first there's a guy from Galveston, Texas, named Barney Richmond, and then another guy from New York named Thomas (inaudible). So I might not have been in the band.

98.t: Key men in the DeLisa band
98.s: Sonny Cohn, Earl Washington, Walter Cole, Porter Kilbert, Harlan Floyd, Johnnie Board, Gene Ammons, Cy Touff, Dennis Farnon and Marty Martinez.
98.ch: Big band, Chicago players, recordings and gospel
98.q: Right, right, right. And so we had he and Harlan Floyd, Booby, he went with Basie, he worked with me, Johnnie Board. And it was just so many musicians that went through the band, and then Gene, Gene would come in and play with us occasionally, Gene Ammons. Yeah, he worked with us at times.

112.t: The six-piece band at Baron Wilkins
112.s: He lists Elmer Chambers, Charley Dixon, Roland Smith, Walter Edwards and Joey Young, and tells about trombonists Revis Horton and Jimmy Harrison.
